answer: Attesters must sit at graph distance at least three from the identity they vouch for, so colluding clusters can't simply mirror each other's endorsements. Every attestation carries a staked bond, and a challenge that proves the pair shares a whisper network of common neighbors slashes both bonds. An attacker must therefore grow a genuinely diverse, costly social graph—not a hollow shell of self-endorsements—making each fake identity pay compounding stake plus the expense of recruiting independent, distance-qualified nodes.
